transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
NVIDIA's board has reinstated Jensen Wong as the company's CEO.
Wong resigned earlier this month due to multiple affairs, including with a possible Chinese spy.
NPR's Stephen Besaha reports President Trump said hiring Wong would be the best move for the country.
NVIDIA is at the center of the artificial intelligence industry,
not only because it provides advanced computer chips needed to develop AI,
but also because it acts like a bank providing loans for other AI companies.
NVIDIA's stock has been plummeting ever since Wong's ouster two weeks ago.
NVIDIA's board sent out a press release saying senior levels of the U.S. government
convinced them Wong is not a national security risk.
That said, the board will continue supporting an independent investigation
into whether Wong was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
After the reinstatement, President Trump wrote on social media congratulating Wong
and called him a great patriot.
Stephen Besaha, NPR News.
The Democratic National Committee has announced its debate schedule for the party's 2028 nominating contest.
And as NPR's Tamara Keith reports, it starts soon.
The dust has barely settled on the 2026 midterms, but the DNC is on to the next race
and what is expected to be a very large field of Democratic presidential hopefuls.
A framework released by the party calls for 12 presidential primary debates
with the first coming in June and July of next year.
In politics, life comes at you fast.
The plan suggests early debates could be divided over two nights
with a maximum of 20 candidates across both nights.
In order to avoid a kids' table effect, the candidates will be randomly selected
rather than having all the front runners on one night.
Tamara Keith, NPR News.
The lawyer for the father and daughter pulled from a crowded C-TAC airport jetway
by ICE agents over the weekend says they were here legally.
Kate Stone from member station KUOW has the latest.
Now, viral video shows agents wrestling Ricardo Lorondo Mendoza and Sofia Hernandez Meija to the floor
while they were trying to board an Alaska Airlines flight on Saturday.
Homeland Security says both overstayed visas and Meija will face a felony charge
for allegedly throwing hot coffee.
But their attorney, Olia Catala, says both hold valid work permits
and are allowed to live in the U.S. while awaiting pending asylum and green card decisions.
Congress created these legal pathways. Sofia and her father were using them.
Washington Governor Bob Ferguson says state officials are reviewing
whether agents violated a state law passed in March
banning law enforcement officers from wearing masks.
For NPR News, I'm Kate Stone in Seattle.
On Wall Street, the Dow is up more than 1,400 points.
The Nasdaq is up more than 1,500.
You're listening to NPR News.
Beijing is urging the Federal Communications Commission to rescind its recent ban
enacted on Chinese telecom companies.
NPR's Jennifer Pak reports the FCC cites national security threats.
The FCC voted to bar Chinese telecom firms, including China Mobile and China Unicom,
from directly accessing U.S. phone numbers.
It's an attempt to stop illegal robocalls.
And part of a wider concern about China potentially using U.S. telecoms for spying.
The FCC decision came just hours after President Trump called Chinese leader Xi Jinping a friend
during a visit to China last week.
Such action by the FCC runs counter to what the two leaders agreed on
and undermines U.S.-China stability, says the Chinese Commerce Ministry,
and warns it will retaliate if the U.S. ban is not rescinded.
Jennifer Pak, NPR News, Beijing.
The Hunger Games movie franchise has a lot to celebrate.
The movie "Sunrise on the Reaping" debuted with an estimated $120 million
in North American theaters over the weekend.
It brought in $225 million globally.
The previous chapter, "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes," grossed about half as much
as the first four movies of the series.
Amazon MGM Studios' "I Play Rocky" came in second with $9.3 million.
The comic drama about the making of Rocky scored a rare eight-plus cinema score.
It follows Sylvester Stallone's struggle to star as Rocky Balboa in the 1976 film "Rocky."
I'm Linda Kenyon.
NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: NVIDIA's board reinstates CEO Jensen Huang after resignation over affairs and spy concerns
Democratic National Committee releases 2028 presidential primary debate framework with 12 debates
Father and daughter pulled from Alaska Airlines jetway by ICE agents; attorney says they were legal
Chinese government urges FCC to rescind ban on China Mobile and China Unicom phone access
Hunger Games prequel "Sunrise on the Reaping" opens to $120 million in North American theaters
